What is the value of $OG\colon BC$? If $CE = CF$, what is the value of $CF\colon OF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

(1) Since $O$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $OB=OA=OC$, \\
Since $OD$ bisects $\angle AOC$ and intersects $AC$ at point $G$, \\
$\therefore$ point $G$ is the midpoint of $AC$, \\
$\therefore$ $OG$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, \\
$\therefore$ $OG\parallel BC$ and $OG=\frac{1}{2}BC$, that is, $\frac{OG}{BC}=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$; 

(2) \\
Since $OD=OA$, \\
$\therefore$ $OD=OB$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ODB=\angle OBD$, \\
Since $OG\perp AC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle DGE=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle GDE+\angle DEG=90^\circ$, \\
Since $CE=CF$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CEF=\angle CFE$, \\
Since $\angle CEF=\angle DEG$, $\angle CFE=\angle OFB$, and $\angle ODB=\angle OBD$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle OFB+\angle OBD=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle FOB=90^\circ$, that is, $CO\perp AB$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle OBC$ is an isosceles right triangle, \\
$\therefore$ $BC: OB=\sqrt{2}: 1$; 

Knowing from (1) that $OG\parallel BC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BCF\sim \triangle DOF$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CF}{OF}=\frac{BC}{OD}=\frac{BC}{OB}=\boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.
